ic_name: Single Edge Nibble Transmission (SENT, SAE J2716)

derived_from_L2.protocol_overview.label: verdict_byte_offset defaulted to 6 (AID-class half-duplex single-wire convention) — L3 did not extract an offset
expected_verdict_byte_hex defaulted to AID-class protocol PASS sentinel (canonical 0xF2 at byte_offset 6); L3 did not extract a verdict-byte literal — low_confidence

module_role: Single-wire automotive sensor interface controller: a SENT (SAE J2716) transmitter (smart sensor) or receiver (ECU) that encodes/decodes nibble pulses (12 + value ticks, falling-edge timed), frames them with a 56-tick synchronization/calibration pulse, a status nibble, 1-6 data nibbles, and a 4-bit CRC nibble, carries a slow serial channel in the status nibble, and optionally implements the synchronous SENT-SPC master-trigger variant.
topology_description: Point-to-point: one smart sensor drives one ECU over a single signal wire (plus supply and ground). One SENT wire per sensor; no bus, no multi-drop, no addressing in basic mode.

integration_overview.clocking: embedded (tick time from the 56-tick calibration pulse)

interfaces.signal: single SENT signal wire (0 V / 5 V)

interface_categories: Signal interface — single push-pull SENT wire (nibble pulses).
Power interface — supply and ground (three-wire interface).
Frame interface — calibration pulse + status + data + CRC nibbles.
SPC interface — optional ECU master trigger pulse (synchronous).
interconnect_topologies_supported: Point-to-point sensor -> ECU (one wire per sensor).
SENT with optional pause pulse (fixed frame length).
Synchronous SENT-SPC (ECU master trigger, addressable channels).
default_signal_values_when_omitted: The signal line idles high between pulses; in basic SENT the sensor transmits continuously, so an idle wire indicates no sensor or a fault.
soc_dependent_items: Number of data nibbles (1-6) and channel format.
Pause-pulse enable and target frame length.
Slow-channel content (Short vs Enhanced serial message).
device_classes_examples: SENT smart sensor (pressure / position / mass-air-flow) — transmitter
